learningObjectives.title: The British Sector of the Western Front and WWI medicine, 1914-18

questions.q: The Theory of the Four Humours held that the body contained blood, phlegm, yellow bile and which fourth humour?
questions.explain: The four humours were blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile, which were believed to need to be kept in balance for good health.

questions.q: Which ancient physician's Theory of Opposites dominated medieval medical training in Britain?
questions.explain: Galen developed the Theory of Opposites from the Four Humours, and his ideas were preserved and promoted by the Church throughout the Middle Ages.

questions.q: The Black Death first reached Britain in which year?
questions.explain: The Black Death arrived in Britain in 1348, and people commonly blamed God, miasma and an imbalance of the humours.

questions.q: Why did most people in medieval Britain believe disease was caused by miasma?
options: They thought bad air from rotting matter and filth spread illness
They had identified bacteria under microscopes
They believed only in astrology as a cause
They rejected all religious explanations of disease
questions.explain: Miasma theory held that bad or poisonous air given off by decaying matter and waste caused disease.

questions.q: A Renaissance physician following the Theory of Opposites treats a patient with a fever, thought to be caused by too much hot, wet blood. What treatment would he most likely choose?
options: Bleeding the patient to remove excess blood
Feeding the patient hot, spicy foods
questions.explain: The Theory of Opposites treated an excess of a humour by removing it, so bleeding was used to reduce a supposed excess of hot, wet blood.

questions.q: Why was Andreas Vesalius's 'The Fabric of the Human Body' (1543) significant?
options: It corrected mistakes in Galen's anatomy through careful dissection
It proved the germ theory of disease
It established the National Health Service
questions.explain: Vesalius used human dissection to correct errors in Galen's anatomy, encouraging others to question established authority.

questions.q: William Harvey is best known for proving which discovery in 1628?
options: The circulation of the blood around the body
questions.explain: Harvey demonstrated that the heart pumps blood in a one-way circulation around the body, challenging Galen's ideas.

questions.q: Edward Jenner developed his smallpox vaccination in 1796 using material taken from which disease?
questions.explain: Jenner noticed milkmaids who caught cowpox did not get smallpox, and used cowpox matter to vaccinate James Phipps.

questions.q: Why was Louis Pasteur's Germ Theory (1861) a turning point in medicine?
options: It showed that microbes in the air cause decay and disease, not miasma
It proved the Four Humours were correct
questions.explain: Pasteur's Germ Theory established that microorganisms cause decay and disease, replacing older ideas like spontaneous generation and miasma.

questions.q: Which scientist identified the specific microbes causing tuberculosis (1882) and cholera (1883)?
questions.explain: Robert Koch developed methods to identify specific bacteria and linked particular microbes to specific diseases such as TB and cholera.

questions.q: How did John Snow's 1854 investigation of the Broad Street pump advance ideas about cholera?
options: It provided evidence that cholera spread through contaminated water, not bad air
It proved cholera was caused by an imbalance of humours
It led directly to the discovery of penicillin
questions.explain: Snow mapped cholera deaths around the Broad Street pump and showed the disease spread through contaminated water, challenging miasma theory.

questions.q: Joseph Lister introduced which substance in 1867 to reduce infection during surgery?
questions.explain: Inspired by Germ Theory, Lister used carbolic acid to kill microbes on wounds and instruments, pioneering antiseptic surgery.

questions.q: A government wants to reduce cholera by cleaning up water supplies in the 1870s. Which measure best reflects this aim?
options: Passing the 1875 Public Health Act requiring clean water and sewers
questions.explain: The 1875 Public Health Act made local authorities provide clean water, drainage and sewers, reflecting acceptance of Germ Theory and public health responsibility.

questions.q: Alexander Fleming is credited with discovering which substance in 1928?
questions.explain: Fleming observed that Penicillium mould killed bacteria on a culture plate, discovering the antibiotic penicillin.

questions.q: Why were Howard Florey and Ernst Chain essential to the success of penicillin?
options: They developed methods to purify and mass-produce it as a usable drug
They first observed the mould killing bacteria
They discovered the structure of DNA
They founded the National Health Service
questions.explain: Florey and Chain purified penicillin and, with US backing during WWII, enabled its mass production for treating patients.

questions.q: The National Health Service was established in Britain in which year?
questions.explain: The NHS was set up in 1948 under Aneurin Bevan, providing healthcare free at the point of use.

questions.q: Why is the term 'magic bullet' used for Salvarsan 606 and Prontosil?
options: They were chemical drugs that targeted and killed specific bacteria causing a disease
They were the first anaesthetics used in surgery
They were vaccines that prevented smallpox
questions.explain: Magic bullets were chemical compounds that attacked the microbe causing a specific disease without harming the rest of the body.

questions.q: In the chain of evacuation on the Western Front, where was most major surgery and triage carried out?
questions.explain: Casualty Clearing Stations were large enough for major operations and used triage to sort wounded soldiers by priority.

questions.q: How did the Thomas splint improve survival on the Western Front from around 1916?
options: It kept a fractured leg rigid, sharply reducing deaths from broken femurs
It filtered poison gas from the air
questions.explain: The Thomas splint immobilised fractured legs, dramatically raising survival rates for soldiers with broken femurs.

questions.q: A soldier at the Battle of Cambrai in 1917 needs a blood transfusion during surgery. Which recent development made stored blood available?
options: Using sodium citrate and refrigeration to store blood in a blood bank
The invention of the Thomas splint
questions.explain: Adding sodium citrate stopped blood clotting and allowed chilled blood to be stored, enabling a blood bank at Cambrai in 1917.
